cap.peripherals.missing: Keyboard and mouse sharing is done by Deskflow, which is not installed.

cap.private_network.ok: Tailscale is installed: paired computers and servers are reachable from anywhere, privately.
cap.servers.missing: Home and Cloud servers are reached over SSH, which is not installed.

cap.shared_clipboard.missing: The clipboard travels with the shared keyboard and mouse, which needs Deskflow.
cap.shared_clipboard.ok: Text and images copied on one computer can be pasted on the other.
cap.shared_clipboard.wayland: Text is shared. On Wayland, images and files may not be, depending on the desktop.
cap.terminal_clipboard.ok: Copying inside a server session reaches this computer's clipboard (OSC 52, through WezTerm).
cap.terminal_clipboard.partial: Copying from a server session to this computer depends on the terminal. WezTerm supports it; many built-in terminals do not.
cap.workspace.ok: A normal folder on this computer. It works without any other component.
cap.workstation_layout.gnome: Editor, terminal and browser open on their own workspaces (GNOME, through a small helper extension).
cap.workstation_layout.hammerspoon_missi: Your tools are opened for you. Arranging them on Spaces and the global shortcut use Hammerspoon, which is not installed.
cap.workstation_layout.hammerspoon_permi: Your tools are opened for you. Arranging them on Spaces and the global shortcut use Hammerspoon, which needs Accessibility permission.
cap.workstation_layout.other_desktop: Your tools are opened for you. Placing each window on its own workspace is implemented for GNOME only; on {desktop} the windows open where the desktop puts them.
cap.workstation_layout.this_desktop: Your tools are opened for you. Placing each window on its own workspace is implemented for GNOME only; on this desktop the windows open where the desktop puts them.
cap.workstation_layout.windows: Your tools are opened for you. Arranging windows on virtual desktops and a global shortcut are not implemented on Windows yet.

install.deskflow.linux: Install Deskflow from Flathub (org.deskflow.deskflow) or your distribution.

mode.leave_text: Choose what happens to the windows this mode opened. Windows you opened yourself are never closed.
network.text: Computers on the same home or office network connect directly. For everywhere else the product uses a private network you already have, such as Tailscale; it never needs a public address or an account with us.

permission.macos.accessibility.effect: This Mac can be controlled from, and can control, your other paired computers. Nothing is recorded.

permission.windows.firewall.title: Windows Firewall (private networks)
permission.windows.firewall.what: An allow rule for file sync and keyboard/mouse sharing on private networks.
permission.windows.firewall.why: Other paired computers on your home or office network connecting to this one.

problem.pairing_code_invalid.fix: Copy the whole code again from the other computer.
problem.pairing_code_invalid.what: That pairing code can not be used.
problem.pairing_code_invalid.why: It is incomplete, mistyped, or not a pairing code.
problem.pairing_merge_unconfirmed.fix: Tick the box to confirm the merge, or cancel.
problem.pairing_not_ready.what: This computer has nothing to pair yet.
problem.pairing_not_ready.why: Neither file sync nor keyboard sharing is set up.
problem.pairing_number_mismatch.fix: Compare the six digits on both screens. If they differ, do not pair.
problem.pairing_number_mismatch.why: Either it was mistyped, or the code came from a different computer than the one in front of you.
problem.peripherals_not_started.what: Keyboard and mouse sharing did not start.
problem.project_not_planned.what: That project can not be sent.
problem.repair_failed.fix: Open the details, or export a support bundle from Health.
problem.repair_failed.why: Your files and settings are unchanged.
problem.server_auth_required.fix: Add this computer's key on the server, then test again.
problem.server_auth_required.why: The key or password this computer uses is not accepted there.
problem.server_not_configured.what: That server is not set up.
problem.server_offline.fix: Everything on this computer keeps working. Try again when the server is back.
problem.server_offline.why: It may be switched off or unreachable from this network.
problem.server_unreachable.fix: Check the address and that the server is running, then try again.
problem.server_unreachable.why: The address may be wrong, the server may be off, or a network may be blocking the connection.
problem.server_untrusted.fix: Edit the address and check the server identity.
problem.server_untrusted.what: {role}: the server identity is not confirmed.
problem.snapshot_not_restored.why: It is damaged or no longer exists. Your current settings are unchanged.
problem.sync_not_running.what: The sync service did not respond.
problem.sync_not_set_up.fix: Run the repair for file sync in Health.
problem.sync_not_set_up.what: File sync is not set up on this computer.
problem.terminal_not_opened.fix: Choose a terminal in Settings → Terminal.
problem.terminal_not_opened.what: A terminal window could not be opened.
problem.title: Something did not work
problem.transfer_failed.fix: Try again; it continues where it stopped.
problem.transfer_failed.why: Nothing was removed on either side.
problem.transfer_unconfirmed.fix: Review the warnings and tick the box to confirm.
problem.transfer_unconfirmed.why: It is large, or contains files that look like credentials.
problem.unexpected.fix: Try again. If it keeps happening, export a support bundle from Health and report it.
problem.unexpected.what: The application ran into a problem it did not expect.
problem.unexpected.why: Nothing was changed by the step that failed.
problem.unknown_request.what: That action is not available in this version.
problem.update_rejected.fix: Nothing was installed. Try again later.
problem.update_rejected.why: It could not be downloaded, or it did not match its published checksum and was deleted.
problem.user_invalid.what: That is not a valid user name.
problem.version_not_restored.what: That version could not be restored.
problem.window_disconnected.fix: Close this window and open the application again.
problem.window_disconnected.what: This window lost its connection to the application.
problem.window_disconnected.why: The application was closed or restarted.
recovery.app_lead: Verified installers are kept on this computer, so you can go back to an earlier version without Internet.
recovery.config_broken: A settings file is damaged. The application is running on the last version that worked.
recovery.export_devices: Include paired computers and server addresses
recovery.export_devices_help: Public identities and addresses. Never passwords.
recovery.export_machine_help: Name, folder locations, local ports — for a full backup of this computer only.
recovery.export_secrets: Passwords, keys and tokens are never exported. They stay in this computer's credential store.
recovery.export_text: Saves your settings to a file you can import on another computer.
recovery.files_lead: Replaced and deleted files are kept for {days} days. This works without Internet.
recovery.import_secrets: {n} saved passwords are referenced but not included; you will be asked for them when they are needed.
recovery.import_text: Choose a settings file exported from this product.
recovery.lead: Ways back: earlier file versions, earlier settings, and a clean way out.
recovery.no_installers: No installers have been downloaded yet.
recovery.nothing_changed: Nothing outside the application's own folders was changed.
recovery.reset_text: Settings return to their defaults. Paired computers, servers and all files are kept, and a snapshot is taken first.
recovery.restore_text: Settings go back to this snapshot. The current settings are saved as a new snapshot first.
recovery.settings_lead: A snapshot is taken automatically before every change to your settings.
recovery.uninstall_how: Uninstall from your system's usual place (Apps, Applications, Software). It asks whether to keep these settings.
recovery.uninstall_lead: See exactly what uninstalling removes and what it leaves, before you decide.
repair.background.text: Starts any background component that should be running and is not.
repair.config.text: Replaces unreadable settings files with the last version that worked. The damaged file is kept.
repair.done.running: every background component is already running
repair.integration.text: Restores the shortcut, the launcher entry and the server names.
repair.peripherals.text: Rewrites the sharing profile and restarts it.
repair.service.text: Reinstalls and restarts the background service.
repair.state.text: Checks the application's own state files and restores them from their backups.
repair.sync.text: Recreates the sync configuration and restarts the service. Files are not touched.
security.host_check_on: Always on; can not be switched off
security.no_store: No system credential store found — passwords are not saved
servers.already_trusted: You already confirmed this exact identity earlier.
servers.cloud_lead: A rented machine for heavy work. It receives only the projects you choose to send, never the whole work folder.
servers.degraded: This server is reached over a public address rather than a private network. It works, but a private network such as Tailscale is safer.
servers.fingerprint_how: Compare it with the fingerprint shown in your provider's console, or on the server itself. Continue only if they match.
servers.fingerprint_text: The server identified itself with this fingerprint:
servers.form_lead: Enter how this computer reaches the server. You can change it later without touching anything else.
servers.home_lead: An always-on computer of yours — a mini server, a NAS, a spare PC — that keeps a second copy of the work folder and can run small services.
servers.identity_changed: Warning: this address previously belonged to a server with a different identity. If you did not reinstall or replace the server, someone may be intercepting the connection. Cancel unless you are sure.
servers.lead: Servers are optional. Each has a name — Home, Cloud — so an address can change without anything else changing.
servers.no_ssh: OpenSSH is not installed on this computer, so servers can not be reached yet. See Health for how to install it.
servers.optional: Not set up. Everything else works without it.
servers.remove_text: Only the connection from this computer is removed. Nothing on the server is deleted.
servers.replace_note: The current Cloud server stays active until the new one has passed every check. If any step fails, nothing changes.
servers.settings_text: Server addresses, sign-in and health live on the Servers page.

settings.sync.fetch_seconds.label: Check repository remotes every
settings.sync.policy.help: “manual” stops and asks. History is never overwritten.
settings.sync.policy.label: When histories diverge
settings.sync.push.label: Push commits automatically
settings.updates.auto_check.help: One request to the release page. Nothing about you is sent.
settings.updates.auto_check.label: Check for updates daily
settings.updates.channel.label: Update channel

settings.work.enabled.label: Keep the work folder in sync
settings.work.git_autosync.label: Also for repositories inside the work folder

snapshot.reason.before-cloud-remove: before the Cloud server was removed
snapshot.reason.before-home-remove: before the Home server was removed
snapshot.reason.before-migration: before an update of the settings format
support.text: Creates a zip file you can attach to a bug report. Names and addresses are replaced by placeholders; it contains no work files, passwords, keys or tokens. Review it before sharing.
sync.conflicts_lead: When the same file changes on two computers before they sync, both versions are kept. Choose the one to keep; the other goes to the application's trash, not away.
sync.errors: Files that could not be synced
sync.lead: Files in the work folder are sent directly between your paired computers.
sync.no_peers: No other computer is paired yet. Sync starts as soon as you pair one.
sync.reason.conflicts: In sync, with conflicts to review.
sync.reason.in_sync: Every paired computer has the same files.
sync.reason.no_peer: Ready. No other computer is paired yet.
sync.reason.not_configured: File sync has not been set up on this computer.
sync.reason.not_installed: File sync needs Syncthing, which is not installed.
sync.reason.peer_offline: This computer is up to date; the other one is offline.
sync.reason.stopped: The sync service is not running.
sync.restore_note: Restoring never overwrites: if a file with that name exists, the restored copy gets a new name.
sync.versions_lead: Files replaced or deleted from another computer are kept here: {n} right now.
toast.conflict_kept: Done. The other version is in the application's trash.
toast.migration_failed: Your settings could not be upgraded to the new format, so the previous format is still in use. Nothing was lost.
uninstall.kept.passwords: passwords in the system credential store
uninstall.kept.servers: files on your Home and Cloud servers
updates.downloaded_text: The installer matched its published checksum. Open it to install; your settings and files are kept. The folder with the file was opened for you.
updates.trust: An update is used only if it matches the checksum published with the release; the installer's signature is then verified by your operating system. Nothing is installed without you.
wizard.cloud.title: Cloud server
wizard.components.lead: The application builds on well-known tools. It uses what is installed and tells you plainly what is not.
wizard.components.note: Nothing here is required to continue. Missing tools only switch off the feature that needs them.
wizard.components.title: What is available on this computer
wizard.finish.personal: This computer is set up as a Personal computer. Your work folder is ready, and nothing runs in the background.
wizard.finish.title: All set
wizard.finish.workstation: Your workstation is ready. Enter Workstation Mode from the overview whenever you sit down to work.
wizard.home.title: Home server
wizard.integration.desktop.text: A keyboard shortcut for Workstation Mode and an entry in your application launcher.
wizard.integration.shell.text: A marked block in your shell start-up file.
wizard.integration.ssh.text: Lets “ssh home” and “ssh cloud” work. Adds one line to your SSH configuration, inside a marked block.
wizard.integration.terminal.text: WezTerm settings that make copying work across server sessions. Only if you have no WezTerm configuration yet.
wizard.kind.lead: You can change this later. Nothing is installed or changed until the last step.
wizard.kind.personal.text: A normal desktop. The application stays out of the way: no shortcuts, no background service, no changes to your system.
wizard.kind.title: How will you use this computer?
wizard.kind.workstation.text: A work folder that syncs between your computers, a shared keyboard and mouse, and optional servers.
wizard.optional: Optional. You can do this later from the main window.
wizard.pair.lead: Install the application on your other computer, then pair the two with a code.
wizard.pair.title: Pair another computer
wizard.permissions.lead: Nothing has been changed yet. This is the complete list.
wizard.permissions.title: What will change on this computer
wizard.permissions.undo: Every file is backed up before it is touched, and everything listed here can be undone from Recovery.
wizard.selftest.title: System check
wizard.setup.autostart: Start in the background when I sign in
wizard.setup.autostart.text: So sync keeps working without opening this window.
wizard.setup.lead: Sensible defaults are selected. Change anything you like.
wizard.setup.peripherals.text: Uses Deskflow, over your private network only.
wizard.setup.sync: Sync the work folder between my computers
wizard.setup.sync.text: Uses Syncthing. Files travel directly between your computers.
wizard.setup.title: Recommended setup
wizard.welcome.existing: An earlier setup was found on this computer. Your settings and folders are kept; this assistant only confirms them.
wizard.welcome.text: Turn your computers into one coordinated workspace.
wizard.welcome.title: Welcome to {name}
wizard.workspace.existing: This folder already contains {n} items. They are kept exactly as they are.
wizard.workspace.lead: Everything you put in this folder can be shared with your other computers.
wizard.workspace.note: System folders, credentials and your whole home folder can not be chosen: they belong to this computer only.
wizard.workspace.title: Choose your work folder
workspace.boundary: What is shared and what stays here
workspace.boundary_lead: Everything inside the work folder is shared — including hidden files and project settings. This computer's own identity never is.
workspace.change_text: Use “{path}” as the work folder? Files in the previous folder stay where they are; they are not moved.
workspace.large_lead: Files above {mb} MB are held back and listed here instead of being sent without asking. Nothing is moved or deleted.
workspace.lead: One folder that is the same on every computer you pair.
workspace.local_text: System passwords, SSH host keys, private-network identity, sign-in sessions and this computer's own identity. They live outside the work folder and are never offered for sharing.
workspace.shared_text: Source, documents, hidden files, .env files you keep with a project, project keys and certificates, assistant instructions and project context.
workspace.skipped_lead: Folders that every computer rebuilds for itself — caches, installed dependencies and Git's internal data — stay local.
workstations.caps_lead: Operating systems differ. This is what works here, detected rather than assumed.
workstations.lead: Computers you paired trust each other. Nothing on your network is trusted automatically.
workstations.name_rule: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, for example: studio-laptop.
